findings.source_quote: τούτοις οὖν ἐστὶ μετάνοια, ἐὰν ταχὺ μετανοήσωσι καὶ μὴ ἐπιμείνωσι ταῖς ἡδοναῖς αὐτῶν
findings.english_quote: The selected 1891 clause lacks explicit “still” (eti), unlike paragraph 3; the supplied comparison reports that Michigan explicitly has “still,” Bonner printed p. 109.
findings.issue: The main text correctly omits “still,” but note d inaccurately characterizes the supplied comparison evidence. The supplied records discuss the continuity and conditional scope of Michigan's paragraph 5 without explicitly reporting ἔτι. Thus the assertion that the supplied comparison reports this particular word is unsupported by the supplied records. This does not establish that the attributed Michigan reading is false.
findings.suggested_revision: Supply a bounded transcription or comparison excerpt documenting ἔτι at the cited location, including whether it is preserved or editorially supplied. Alternatively, revise the note to distinguish the edition-attributed reading from what the supplied comparison actually documents. Retain the selected main-text reading; any revised note requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τούτοις οὖν ἐστὶ μετάνοια, ἐὰν ταχὺ μετανοήσωσι καὶ μὴ ἐπιμείνωσι ταῖς ἡδοναῖς αὐτῶν
findings.english_quote: The selected 1891 clause lacks explicit “still” (eti), unlike paragraph 3; the supplied comparison reports that Michigan explicitly has “still,” Bonner printed p. 109.
findings.issue: Independently checked against the Greek, the simplified main text preserves this clause's conditions and correctly omits “still.” Its note nevertheless claims that the supplied comparison explicitly reports Michigan's ἔτι, whereas the supplied records document conditional scope and continuity, not that particular word. The defect is the evidence attribution, not a demonstrated false manuscript reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a bounded excerpt documenting the reported Michigan ἔτι and its preserved or supplied status, or qualify the note so it does not attribute that specific observation to the supplied comparison. Do not insert “still” into the selected main text merely because an alternative is reported. Submit any replacement note for fresh review.

summary: Both editions were independently reviewed against every clause of the selected Greek. No concrete main-text fidelity defect was identified: the rod groups, fractions, repentance conditions, negations, death warnings, and speaker perspective remain intact. The version-supported proportion correction is distinguished from the reported Athos alternative. Both editions need a limited correction or evidentiary supplement to note d's description of the supplied comparison. This review does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify an exhaustive collation.
